name: EWWF World Championship
epitaph: Already held by Adam Mitchell when the surviving record opens on 16 April 2002. Simon Solkoff held it undocumented by Redemption in June, retained through a time-limit draw and a three-way C-4 exploding match at Kingdom of the Wicked, and lost it to Despair in a two-on-one handicap match on 2 October, Adam Mitchell counting the pin himself. Despair retained against Simon Underwood on 10 October before losing it to Harvester of Sorrow in a three-way with Ashlyn Summers on 5 December, the last held broadcast in this run.

name: EWWF United States Championship
epitaph: Held by Smoove when the surviving record opens, changing hands on 16 April 2002 to Thomas Casey. The title cycled repeatedly across the spring and summer among Casey, Jimmy Slade, Axel Reed and Randy Love before Slade's 8 August win; it later passed undocumented to Randy Love and was ruled to Sammy Paulison by disqualification on 10 October, then passed undocumented again to Larry Spikowski, who retained against Ragnarok on 5 December.

name: Surrender Extreme Championship
epitaph: First attested champion Despair won the title from Randy Love in a parking-lot ladder match on 16 April 2002. He lost it around 10 July to Homeless Joe Boxcar (shown only in a later recap) and regained it the same night, 17 July, after Trinity interference. Ashlyn Summers held it undocumented by 8 August, retaining in a hardcore match that night and again at Kingdom of the Wicked; Harvester of Sorrow held it undocumented by 5 December, having already assaulted Summers before that broadcast.
notes: The fed's own broadcasts also call this belt the “Surrender Extreme Championship” and, coarsely, the “Sex Championship”/“EWWF SEX Championship” — the same title under three names in the promotion's own words, confirmed explicitly in its own commentary (“she holds the Surrender Extreme Title...the SEX title”); the registry uses its fullest attested name.

name: EWWF Tag Team Championship
epitaph: Created for an eight-team single-elimination tournament at Kingdom of the Wicked, won by Rune Tao and Liam Zen, who retained the same night against Andrew Krumm and Syko. Jersey City Street Machine (Rocky Camarelli and Sammy Paulison) held the belts undocumented by 2 October before losing them to Ryan Delaney and David Rheaume on 5 December, with help from Nick Demola and the debuting Seventh Seal.

name: EWWF Cruiserweight Championship
epitaph: Already held by Tommy Kain when the surviving record shows it, at Kingdom of the Wicked, where he retained in a triple threat against Ash and David Rheaume. The EWWF office voided the title by decree on 10 October 2002, stripping Kain and voiding Vinnie Cepacelli's own standing as number-one contender, with a successor title promised for the unheld “To Hell and Back.”

name: SEWF Championship
epitaph: A sixteen-man tournament the EWWF ran entirely on its own broadcasts across October 2002 for a title its own ring introductions and commentary call the “SEWF Championship,” “SEWF World Title” and “SEWF Heavyweight Championship.” Tommy Kain won the tournament's final at the unheld “To Hell and Back,” then retained on 5 December against Jimmy Slade after Simon Underwood, the triple threat's third man, was pulled from the match before the bell by Slade's own attack.
notes: This title shares its name and lineage words with the historical, closed sewf promotion's own World Heavyweight Championship (sewf-world) but is never shown as staged, sanctioned or administered by that promotion — the EWWF runs, judges and crowns it on its own shows throughout. Filed as a distinct title belonging to ewwf-surrender-2002; the sewf promotion's own registry row and its own title's reign history are untouched. Flagged for further review given the shared name.
